newsitem.title: NIGERIA: New Nigerian bourse chief upbeat about the future.
newsitem.headline: New Nigerian bourse chief upbeat about the future.

text.p: The Nigerian stock exchange can consider itself one of the important emerging markets, according to its new president.
"The Nigerian stock exchange has arrived," Goodie Ibru, who was elected to the position on Tuesday, told reporters.
He said with the introduction of investor-friendly measures recently, the market had positioned itself to play a more active role in providing long-term funds for Nigeria's development.

Ibru, a lawyer and businessman who is also chairman of an hotels group that owns the Lagos Sheraton Hotel, said eventual growth of the economy in Africa's most populous nation depended on the development of the stock exchange.
"The commissioning of the central securities clearing system (CSCS) is an important and remarkable achievement which ensures our market has been internationalised," he said.
The automated clearing system, designed to speed up market transactions and boost activities, was commissioned on April 7.
Ibru joined his predecessor, Pascal Dozie, in calling on the Nigerian government to speed up the privatisation of state parastatals.
The local business community and multilateral finance bodies expected a major statement on the issue following promises from senior officials of the military government last year.
They were, however, disappointed when the government announced during this year's budget presentation in January that it would set up a committee to look more closely at privatisation.
No such committee has so far been constituted although a visiting World Bank official said on Monday the government was determined to resume privatisation soon.
Ibru said privatisation would create an avenue for foreign fund managers to invest in the Nigerian capital market.
"If we want to invite foreign investors to our market, there must be shares for them to buy," he added.
